title: Omnichannel Contact Center LLM Integration: SOW & Capacity/Pricing Sketch
content:
PURPOSE:
This doc is a working sketch for a customer POC and SOW to integrate a Redwood-hosted LLM for an omnichannel contact center (voice + chat + email routing and agent assist). It captures proposed scope, workshop plan, capacity assumptions, staffing and three pricing models (time & materials, fixed-price POC, and subscription pilot).

BACKGROUND / CONTEXT:
- Customer: mid-market telco contact center (50K monthly chats, 200 agents, peak concurrency ~400).
- Objective: reduce average handle time (AHT) and improve first-contact resolution by surfacing model suggestions to agents, generating draft replies for email, and extracting entity-level metadata from conversations for routing and reporting.
- Constraint: customer requires PII redaction at ingestion and retention controls; they prefer a hybrid routing fallback to smaller quantized models for cheap responses.

ASSUMPTIONS (validate in kickoff):
- We'll use Redwood Hosted API for initial POC; Dedicated capacity recommended for pilot/production.
- Typical session: 5–7 exchanges, average tokens per exchange (request+response) = 600 tokens.
- Peak concurrent inferences during business hours: 400; baseline concurrency for POC = 60 (simulated load).
- Customer will provide representative sample transcripts and sandbox access to their chat/telephony system (e.g., Twilio Flex or Genesys Cloud).
- Security: TLS, customer-managed API keys, and access logs; HSM/KMS integration for pilot is out of POC scope but priced separately.

SCOPE - POC (6 weeks recommended):
1) Workshop & requirements alignment (1 week)
   - 2 half-day working sessions (architecture + data/samples review)
   - Confirm success metrics: AHT reduction target, suggestion acceptance rate, latency SLO (95th pct <= 600ms for agent assist).
2) Integration adapters (2 weeks)
   - Chat adapter: webchat -> Redwood API (streaming responses + tool calls)
   - Telephony adapter: transcript ingestion pipeline (speech-to-text handled by customer) -> Redwood API for assist and summaries
   - Email draft generator (batch inference flow)
3) Prompt engineering & guardrails (1 week)
   - Create 8 canonical prompt templates for agent assist, escalation prompts, and email drafts
   - Safety/PII redaction heuristics and post-processing
4) Test harness & load script (1 week)
   - Simulate 60 concurrent sessions, run synthetic traffic, collect latency/cost metrics
5) Evaluation & handoff (1 week)
   - Run evaluation set, produce report (quality vs. cost), and ops runbook for pilot

DELIVERABLES:
- SOW + acceptance criteria, integration checklists, and runbook
- Deployed POC connectors in customer sandbox (chat + email), prompt library, and evaluation report
- Cost/performance baseline and recommended Dedicated configuration for pilot

WORKSHOP AGENDA (kickoff week):
Day 1 AM: Architecture walkthrough (30m), data flows and security constraints (45m), open questions (15m)
Day 1 PM: Success metrics and evaluation dataset selection (90m), sample transcript labeling exercise (30m)
Pre-work (customer): export 2 weeks of anonymized transcripts, call patterns, and sample email threads

RESOURCE PLAN (POC staffing estimate):
- Solutions Eng (lead): 0.2 FTE over 6 weeks – design + client workshops
- Integration Engineer: 0.6 FTE over 6 weeks – adapters, deploys, test harness
- Prompt Engineer: 0.4 FTE over 3 weeks – templates + evals
- SRE/Platform support: 0.1 FTE as-needed (deployment, credentials)
- Customer SME: 0.3 FTE – data, subject matter, and QA

CAPACITY & COST ASSUMPTIONS (rough - refine after sample data):
- Average tokens per full agent-assist call: 600 tokens (client prompts + model response)
- Requests per agent per day: estimated 30 interactions (agent assists + summaries)
- POC load target: simulate 60 concurrent sessions for 2 hours/day during tests
- Redwood hosted cost estimate (for POC traffic): ~ $1,800–$3,200 for test traffic (depends on model family and avg tokens)
- GPU capacity recommendation for pilot (Dedicated): 2x A100-equivalent GPUs (or equivalent vGPU split) with autoscale buffer for bursts to meet 95th pct latency SLO
- Estimated pilot monthly run-rate for 200 agents (production): $15k–$28k (model variant + caching/batching optimizations will adjust)

PRICING OPTIONS (3 alternatives):
A) Time & Materials (T&M) POC
   - Professional services hourly rates: Solutions Eng $220/hr, Integration Eng $180/hr, Prompt Eng $160/hr.
   - Estimated hours: 180 hrs (total across roles) -> professional services ~= $30,000 + Redwood hosted usage (see above).
   - Pros: flexible, easy change control.
   - Cons: scope creep risk; billing cadence monthly.

B) Fixed-price POC (recommended for procurement simplicity)
   - Fixed fee: $45,000 (covers all integration work per scope above, up to 8 weeks and 6 engineering weeks of effort).
   - Includes two workshops, adapter deliverables, prompt library, evaluation report, and 1 month of post-POC support (30 days).
   - Exclusions: premium enterprise features (HSM, extended retention), major scope changes, paid third-party STT costs.

C) Pilot Subscription (production pilot transition)
   - Implementation fee (pilot lift & handoff): $25,000 (reduced if Fixed POC chosen)
   - Monthly Pilot Fee: $12,000–$20,000 (includes Dedicated minimal capacity, 99.9% uptime target, observability retention tier 1)
   - Optional add-ons: HSM/KMS integration ($8k one-time), On-prem connector packaging ($20k one-time), Extended Support (SLA 24/7) $7k/mo

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (for POC success):
- Agent assist suggestion acceptance >= 20% on evaluation dataset OR AHT reduced by >= 7% on sample week
- Latency: 95th percentile agent-assist response <= 600ms in test harness at POC simulated load
- Quality checks: no PII leakage in 500-sample transcripts after redaction pipeline
- Deliverables delivered and deployed to customer sandbox; runbook and evaluation report signed-off by customer

RISKS & MITIGATIONS:
- Risk: STT quality harms downstream model outputs -> Mitigation: require representative STT samples early; fallback to text-only flow for initial runs
- Risk: Customer cannot provide anonymized transcripts -> Mitigation: use synthetic/seeded dataset and extend workshop for more labeling time
- Risk: Latency spikes during peak -> Mitigation: enable caching (KV/prefix), request batching, and model fallbacks (smaller model for trivials)

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs:
- Confirm which telephony provider and whether we can use webhooks for near-real-time transcripts (JIRA-CC-INT-87).
- Customer preference for Hosted vs Dedicated for pilot? (security review ongoing).
- Identify compliance owner for PI/retention policies.
- Need STT cost estimate from customer (speech->text outsourced).

NEXT STEPS (immediate):
- Schedule kickoff workshop (target: next Tue/Thu) -> action: Asha to send calendar invites and prep deck
- Customer to provide sample transcripts and email threads (anonymized) by EOD week
- Solutions Eng to draft fixed-price SOW (this doc as baseline) and shared procurement checklist

NOTES TO SELF (informal):
- Keep prompt templates small to reduce token consumption; test a 2-turn fallback where agent chooses to expand suggestions.
- Consider recommending Redwood Optimize audit post-POC to tune batching/caching to reduce per-token cost.

APPENDIX - Rough cost calc (example):
- Simulated POC run: 10k interactions * 600 tokens avg = 6M tokens -> hosted cost ballpark $0.0025–$0.006/token -> $1,500–$3,600 (model-dependent)
- Pro tip: use short-turn summaries and local prefix caching to cut tokens by ~25% for agent flows.

End of sketch.
